name: Subtitle Retimer
overview: Finds subtitles for your shows and films and fixes their timing.
description: A page that lists your shows and gets a subtitle for an episode from Jimaku or OpenSubtitles. A model picks the file, and your own Retimer API server can retime it against the video's own subtitle tracks or its audio. The subtitle is saved next to the video and Jellyfin lists it at once.

versions.changelog:
Seasons that a source splits into parts are found.

- When a source keeps one season of your library as several entries, one for each part, the model now chooses all of them. Season 17 of Bleach (Thousand-Year Blood War) is four entries on Jimaku, and before this version the plugin found no subtitle for it. The same goes for seasons such as Attack on Titan's third (two entries) or the first of SPY x FAMILY.
- The model is told the season's own name, how many episodes it has and when they aired, and reads Jimaku's notes on each entry, which often say which episodes it holds. When the notes show that the chosen entries miss episodes of the season, the model is asked once more.
- Jimaku is also searched for the show's title together with the season's name.
- The files of every part are matched to the season's episodes together, also when a part counts its episodes from 1 again.
- When the model matches files for only the first few episodes of a season, it is asked once more for the rest.
- A season that gets a later episode has its entries chosen again, as a new part is often a new entry. An entry you chose yourself stays.
- What the model chose for a season in an earlier version is asked again once, so a season that found nothing before is looked for again.
- The list of files names every entry a season uses.

Watch mode: shows and seasons get their subtitles by themselves.

- "Watch this show" on a show's page fetches the subtitle of each episode as soon as a source has it, for every season and the seasons added later. Each season has a switch of its own, so you can watch only the season that airs. A film can be watched too. A watched show has an eye on its poster.
- Jellyfin runs the check every 3 hours as its own scheduled task, "Check watched shows for subtitles", and a show is checked a few minutes after it gets a new episode. A check starts a job only when a source lists a file that was not tried yet.
- An episode is looked for for 30 days after it came, or after its season was switched on. The settings change the number, and "Watch new shows" watches every show that comes into the library from then on.
- Activity has a second tab, Watching: what is watched, which episodes still wait, and how the last check went.

The project's public home.

- The plugin lives at github.com/friedrich-de/jellyfin-subtitle-retimer and Retimer API at github.com/friedrich-de/subtitle-retimer. The settings page links there.
- Requests to Jimaku and OpenSubtitles name the plugin `jellyfin-subtitle-retimer`.

The page can be installed as an app.

- Chrome, Edge and other browsers built on Chromium offer to install the page at /Retimer as an app. It opens in its own window with its own icon. Installing needs the page to be opened over HTTPS, or at localhost.
- The page has an icon of its own in the browser tab: a stopwatch over two subtitle lines.
- The installed app opens Jellyfin in the browser, and goes on by itself once you sign in to Jellyfin there.
- A service worker keeps a copy of the page's own files, so the app still opens and says so when the server cannot be reached. It never keeps an answer of the server.

Keys are stored encrypted.

- The API keys and the OpenSubtitles password are encrypted in the plugin's settings file and read back only for the call that sends them. The secret that encrypts them is a file of its own in Jellyfin's data folder (`data/subtitle-retimer/settings.key`), readable only by the user Jellyfin runs as. Keys stored in plain by 0.4.0.0 are encrypted at the first start.
- Settings copied from another server lose their keys, because only the server that encrypted them can read them: enter them again on the settings screen. The same goes for a step back to 0.4.0.0.
- The page keeps every call on its own server, whatever address it was opened under, and OpenSubtitles may only move the login to one of its own hosts.

The first public release, for Jellyfin 12.4.

- A page at /Retimer for every signed-in user: your shows with their posters, a show's episodes with their subtitle state, a file picker, the activity of jobs, and settings for administrators.
- Gets subtitles from Jimaku and OpenSubtitles. A model through OpenRouter (Haiku 5.5 by default, with your key) picks the entry, matches files to episodes and checks the language.
- Retimes the subtitle with your own Retimer API server against the video's subtitle tracks or its audio, and can read picture subtitles (PGS) into text.
- Saves the subtitle next to the video, and Jellyfin lists it at once.
- Daily limits on jobs and cost.
